references.text: Isaiah prophesies about drawing water with joy from the wells of salvation (Jes 12:3). Jesus fulfills this promise by offering living water that gives eternal life.
God's invitation to all who are thirsty to come to the waters (Jes 55:1) points forward to Jesus' offer of living water that satisfies thirst forever.
The Lord calls himself the fountain of living water (Jer 2:13). Jesus identifies with this fountain by offering water that becomes a spring of eternal life in those who drink.
Jeremiah refers to the Lord as the fountain of living water (Jer 17:13), which supports the idea that Jesus, as the giver of living water, acts in God's role.

Jesus says that whoever comes to him will never hunger, and whoever believes in him will never thirst (Joh 6:35). This expands on the promise from Joh 4:14 that whoever drinks the water he gives will never thirst again.

During the Feast of Tabernacles, Jesus declares that anyone who is thirsty should come to him and drink, and streams of living water will flow from within those who believe (Joh 7:37-39). This expands on the image of the inner spring from Joh 4:14 and connects it with the Holy Spirit.

In the heavenly vision, it is said that the saved will no longer thirst, and the Lamb will lead them to springs of living water (Åp 7:16-17). This is the final fulfillment of the promise never to thirst again.
God promises to give the thirsty drink from the spring of life freely (Åp 21:6). This reflects Jesus' gift of living water that springs up to eternal life.

The Spirit and the bride say, 'Come!' and let anyone who is thirsty come and take the water of life without cost (Åp 22:17). This is the final invitation in the Bible, corresponding with Jesus' offer of living water.
Shortly earlier in his conversation with the Samaritan woman, Jesus mentions God's gift and the living water (Joh 4:10), which provides context for the promise in verse 14.
The Lord promises to pour out water on the thirsty and streams on the dry ground (Jes 44:3), an image of the outpouring of the Spirit connected with the living water Jesus offers.
The promise of eternal life to those who believe (Joh 3:15-16) is the same eternal life that the water Jesus gives springs up to, according to Joh 4:14.
